pattern.crimePattern: rival shopkeeper kills the island agent who took his mobile-money and ferry agencies, and is alibied for the wrong time by a radio play
pattern.notes: Fictional radio station, radio play and episode. The Dholuo line is for the cultural reader to confirm. Mfangano is home to both Suba and Luo families; the cultural reader should advise on names.

ob.text: A neighbour reports the island's shopkeeper, Emmanuel Ochola (52), found dead in the back room of his shop at Sena, Mfangano Island. Neighbours heard "a terrible quarrel and a crash" at about 21:00 on Thursday night.

facts.text: Emmanuel Ochola, shopkeeper and agent, was found dead in his back room at Sena. Neighbours heard "a terrible quarrel and a crash" at about 21:00.
Back room: one head wound. He lies below the battery shelf. Nothing is broken, and there are no pots on the floor.
A heavy 12-volt solar battery lies on the floor beside him, out of its place on the shelf. One corner is marked.
The radio on the shelf was still on in the morning, tuned to Radio Nam Lolwe, its batteries nearly flat.
Radio Nam Lolwe schedule: "Thursday 21:00 — radio play, episode 12".
Episode 12 summary: scene 2, about 21:08–21:12, two brothers quarrel over a boat. "Ka iwacho kamano, to ber idhi!" Then the sound of pots crashing.
Rispa: at about 21:10 she heard two men shouting through the wall, one said "Ka iwacho kamano, to ber idhi!", then a huge crash. She didn't go round until morning.
Rispa was at home next door all evening, listening to the radio play on her own radio.
Selpher: she served Emmanuel supper at 18:30 and ate the same food. She left for her sister's at 19:00; he was well.
Selpher was at her sister's across the hill from 19:20 for the night.
Selpher: Celestine Wandera owes the shop KSh 30,000. Emmanuel shouted at her outside the shop on Tuesday.
Selpher: there is no family link between Jacktone and Emmanuel. "None. Not by blood, not by marriage."
Agency float book: last entry 19:20, a withdrawal, in Emmanuel's hand. Agency hours are 07:00 to 21:00.
Records, the agency line: last transaction at 19:21. Nothing after, though the agency normally works until 21:00.
Owen and the jetty logbook: Jacktone arrived at about 20:40 and waited for his goods until after 21:30. Half the island saw him there at 21:00.
Owen was in the jetty hut all evening with the logbook.
Paul Odera: at about 19:45 he saw Jacktone come out of the back gate of Emmanuel's shop and hurry down the path with a torch.
The back path from the shop's gate to the jetty takes about 50 minutes in the dark.
Appointment letters: Emmanuel became the island's mobile-money agent in March and its ferry-ticket agent in May. Jacktone held both for twelve years before.
A note in the drawer, from Jacktone, September: "You stole my bread."
Mama Grace: Celestine was at choir practice from 18:30 to 21:30. The register is ticked and twenty voices saw her.
Steve's ferry ticket: Sena to Mbita, Wednesday 17 December, 08:00. He has been in Mbita since.
Credit book: Celestine's KSh 30,000 debt, with a repayment plan of 3,000 a week signed by both on Wednesday.
Jacktone gives his fingerprints voluntarily. "Take them. I was at the jetty."
Autopsy: struck once, from above, with a heavy flat-edged object, consistent with the solar battery. Not a fall.
Autopsy: death between 19:00 and 20:15. His stomach holds a meal eaten about an hour before death.
Autopsy: no burns or electrical marks. No signs of poisoning.
Lab: Jacktone's fingerprints are on the battery's carrying handle.
Jacktone: "I was at the jetty from seven o'clock, waiting for my goods."
Jacktone: "When they quarrelled at nine I was at the jetty. Everyone saw me."
Jacktone: "I went to the jetty a bit later, yes. I was walking around. I didn't go to his shop."
Celestine: "I was at choir."
Steve: "I've been in Mbita since Wednesday."
Steve: "Uncle never turned that radio off. Not even to sleep."

interrogations.intro: Jacktone receives you on his shop veranda with a flask of tea. "Terrible. Terrible. When they quarrelled at nine I was at the jetty. Ask anyone."

topics.reply: Twelve years I served this island. Then a letter from Nairobi, and he has my agencies. Yes, I wrote that note. Bread is bread.
A battery? I have bought batteries there a hundred times. Take my fingerprints. Take them. I was at the jetty.

interrogations.intro: Celestine is still in her choir blouse from the morning service rehearsal. "I owe him. Everyone knows I owe him. I was singing."

topics.reply: He shouted at me on Tuesday, yes. On Wednesday he came to my stall and we signed a plan. Three thousand a week. It's in his book.

interrogations.intro: Steve calls back from the Mbita ferry office, his voice breaking. "I'm coming on the first boat. I've been here since Wednesday."

topics.reply: Uncle never turned that radio off. Not even to sleep. Every Thursday, the play. He laughed at the same jokes every week.

interrogations.intro: Rispa holds her shawl tight at her door. "I heard them. God forgive me, I heard them and I didn't go."

topics.reply: His radio? It's always on. Mine too. On Thursday everyone listens to the play. I had mine on that night.

interrogations.intro: Selpher sits on the shop step with her sister's arm around her. "He ate everything on his plate. He was laughing."

topics.reply: Jacktone? No family of ours. None. Not by blood, not by marriage. Only business.

interrogations.intro: Owen runs a finger down the logbook. "Ojuka came for his goods. Late. The boat was late too."

topics.reply: About twenty to nine he came. Out of breath, sweating. I thought he'd run from the trading centre.

For the first time he has nothing ready. "Paul Odera is an old man with old eyes." He looks at the lake and doesn't say anything else.

timeOfDeath.note: From the autopsy and the supper at 18:30; the agency's last transaction is at 19:21.

proof.concludes: The "quarrel and crash" at about 21:10 was scene 2 of the Thursday radio play, word for word, on a radio that never goes off. Nothing in the back room is broken. It tells you nothing about when Emmanuel died.
He ate supper at 18:30 and died about an hour later, between 19:00 and 20:15; his agency, open until 21:00, went silent after 19:21.
Jacktone's alibi covers 21:00, not 19:30. He reached the jetty at about 20:40, and at 19:45 he was seen leaving Emmanuel's back gate, a fifty-minute walk above the jetty.

Jacktone had lost both agencies to Emmanuel, and his prints are on the battery that matches the blow. Jacktone Ojuka struck Emmanuel with a heavy solar battery because Emmanuel had taken the island's agencies from him.

reconstruction.text: This year a letter from Nairobi moves the island's mobile-money agency, and then the ferry-ticket book, from Jacktone's shop to Emmanuel's. In September Jacktone writes: "You stole my bread."
Thursday, 18:30. Emmanuel eats supper with Selpher. At 19:00 she leaves for her sister's. At 19:21 he serves his last agency customer.
About 19:30. Jacktone comes to the back room with one last offer. Emmanuel refuses. Jacktone lifts a solar battery from the shelf and strikes him once.
19:45. He leaves by the back gate with his torch, fast, down the path. At 20:40 he reaches the jetty, out of breath, and waits where half the island can see him.
21:00. The radio play begins. At 21:10, through the wall, two brothers quarrel over a boat and the pots come crashing down. Rispa holds her breath and doesn't go next door.
